Proof Obligations: spec.txt satisfied by semantics.txt

Goal
    Show that the small-step semantics of semantics.txt computes
    exactly the function specified in spec.txt, i.e. that for every
    integer x, the evaluation of abs(x) produces the unique value y
    satisfying properties P1-P3 of spec.txt.

    Proof method (overall): for each x, (i) show evaluation of abs(x)
    terminates in a unique value v (O1-O4), (ii) show v satisfies the
    spec's case identities (O5-O6), (iii) show v >= 0 (O7), and
    (iv) conclude v is the specified value via uniqueness (O8-O9).

    Notation: "x >= 0" abbreviates "x = 0 or x = s(n) for some n >= 0";
    "x < 0" abbreviates "x = -s(n) for some n >= 0".

---------------------------------------------------------------------
O1. WELL-DEFINEDNESS OF THE STEP RELATION
    Label: step-relation-well-defined
    The relation --> is well-defined: each inference rule of
    semantics.txt Sec. 3 is syntactically well-formed and its side
    conditions are satisfiable.

    Decomposition:
    O1.1  Each rule's premises and conclusion are judgements of the
          form e --> e' with e, e' well-formed expressions.
    O1.2  Side conditions of S-AbsPos / S-AbsNeg ("n non-negative")
          are satisfiable (e.g. n = 0), and decidable over Z.
    O1.3  The successor/inverse notation s(n), -s(n) denotes a unique
          integer for each n.

O2. DETERMINISM OF A SINGLE STEP
    Label: step-determinism
    For all e, e1, e2:  e --> e1 and e --> e2  implies  e1 = e2.

    Decomposition:
    O2.1  Case analysis on e: at most one rule matches each syntactic
          shape (literal, abs(e), abs(v), e1 + e2, e1 - e2).
    O2.2  Congruence rules do not overlap with computation rules
          (computation rules apply only when the relevant operand is
          a value; congruence rules only when it is not).
    O2.3  Each matching rule's conclusion fixes the step result
          uniquely.

O3. PROGRESS / NO STUCK STATES
    Label: progress
    Every closed expression e is either a value or there exists e'
    with e --> e'.

    Decomposition:
    O3.1  Values step nowhere (by definition, literals are normal
          forms).
    O3.2  If e = abs(e0), e0 + e1, or e0 - e1 and the relevant
          subexpression can step, a congruence rule applies.
    O3.3  If all operands are values, a computation rule applies:
          the value cases 0, s(n), -s(n) are exhausted by S-AbsZero,
          S-AbsPos, S-AbsNeg (abs), and S-Plus, S-Minus (arithmetic).

O4. TERMINATION / NORMALIZATION
    Label: termination
    Every expression e reduces to a value: there exist v and k such
    that e -->^k v, and every reduction sequence is finite.

    Decomposition:
    O4.1  Define the measure mu(e) = number of operators
          (abs, +, -) in e; mu(e) >= 0.
    O4.2  Congruence rules preserve mu; computation rules decrease mu
          by exactly 1 (verify for S-AbsZero, S-AbsPos, S-AbsNeg,
          S-Plus, S-Minus).
    O4.3  Hence mu strictly decreases along every -->* chain, so all
          chains are finite.
    O4.4  By O3 the chain cannot get stuck before reaching a value.

O5. CORRECTNESS ON NON-NEGATIVE INPUT  (discharges P2 of spec.txt)
    Label: abs-non-negative-case
    For all x in Z:  x >= 0  implies  abs(x) -->* x.

    Decomposition:
    O5.1  Case x = 0:  abs(0) --> 0 by S-AbsZero, hence abs(0) -->* 0.
    O5.2  Case x = s(n), n >= 0:  abs(s(n)) --> s(n) by S-AbsPos,
          hence abs(s(n)) -->* s(n).
    O5.3  The two cases exhaust all x >= 0 (trichotomy on Z).

O6. CORRECTNESS ON NEGATIVE INPUT  (discharges P3 of spec.txt)
    Label: abs-negative-case
    For all x in Z:  x < 0  implies  abs(x) -->* -x.

    Decomposition:
    O6.1  Every x < 0 is uniquely of the form -s(n) with n >= 0.
    O6.2  abs(-s(n)) --> s(n) by S-AbsNeg, hence abs(-s(n)) -->* s(n).
    O6.3  Arithmetic lemma: -(-s(n)) = s(n), i.e. the computed value
          s(n) equals the specified result -x.
    O6.4  Combine O6.2 and O6.3 to conclude abs(x) -->* -x.

O7. NON-NEGATIVITY OF THE RESULT  (discharges P1 of spec.txt)
    Label: result-non-negative
    For all x in Z and all v:  abs(x) -->* v  implies  v >= 0.

    Decomposition:
    O7.1  By O2 (extended to -->*) and O4, v is unique, so it suffices
          to inspect the reductions of O5 and O6.
    O7.2  In O5: v = x >= 0 by assumption.
    O7.3  In O6: v = s(n) with n >= 0, and s(n) >= 0 (successor
          lemma: n >= 0 implies s(n) >= 0).

O8. UNIQUENESS OF THE SPECIFIED VALUE
    Label: spec-characterization-uniqueness
    If y1 and y2 both satisfy P1-P3 of spec.txt for the same x, then
    y1 = y2.

    Decomposition:
    O8.1  Case x >= 0: P2 forces y1 = y2 = x.
    O8.2  Case x < 0:  P3 forces y1 = y2 = -x.
    O8.3  The cases exhaust Z, so at most one value satisfies
          P1-P3 for each x.

O9. SOUNDNESS OF THE GENERAL EVALUATION  (Sec. 6 of semantics.txt)
    Label: denotational-soundness
    For all expressions e and values v:  e -->* v  implies
    [[e]] = v, with [[n]] = n, [[abs(e)]] = |[[e]]|, [[e1 + e2]] =
    [[e1]] + [[e2]], [[e1 - e2]] = [[e1]] - [[e2]].

    Decomposition:
    O9.1  Each computation rule preserves the denotation:
          [[abs(0)]] = [[0]]; [[abs(s(n))]] = [[s(n)]] for n >= 0;
          [[abs(-s(n))]] = [[s(n)]] for n >= 0; [[n1 + n2]] =
          [[n1]] + [[n2]]; [[n1 - n2]] = [[n1]] - [[n2]].
    O9.2  Each congruence rule preserves the denotation ([[ei]] =
          [[ei']] implies [[C[ei]]] = [[C[ei']]] for the three
          contexts abs(.), . + ., . - .).
    O9.3  Induction on the length of the reduction e -->^k v using
          O9.1 and O9.2.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
Derivation of the main theorem
    Label: main-theorem
    For all x in Z, abs(x) -->* y where y is the unique value with
    y = x if x >= 0, y = -x if x < 0, and y >= 0.

    Uses:
    M.1  Existence: O4 (termination) + O3 (progress) give a value y
         with abs(x) -->* y.
    M.2  Uniqueness of y: O2 + O4 (deterministic single steps
         extended to -->*).
    M.3  Case identities: O5 gives P2, O6 gives P3.
    M.4  Non-negativity: O7 gives P1.
    M.5  By O8, y is THE value specified by spec.txt.
    M.6  O9 then yields full agreement with the mathematical
         denotation, closing the soundness claim of semantics.txt.

Dependency sketch
    O1 --> O2, O3
    O2, O3 --> O4
    O2, O4 --> O7.1, M.2
    O5, O6 --> O7, M.3
    O5, O6, O7 --> M.4
    O8 + M.3, M.4 --> M.5
    O9 + M.1 --> M.6
